officialTitle: Adjuvant Chemotherapy Guided by a 21-Gene Expression Assay in Breast Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Of the 9719 eligible patients with follow-up information, 6711 (69%) had a midrange recurrence score of 11 to 25 and were randomly assigned to receive either chemoendocrine therapy or endocrine therapy alone.
primaryEndpoints: Invasive disease-free survival (non-inferiority of endocrine therapy alone)
secondaryEndpoints: Freedom from distant or locoregional recurrence
design.notes: Prospective trial enrolling women with HR+/HER2- node-negative disease; only the midrange recurrence-score cohort was randomised. Low- and high-score cohorts were assigned treatment non-randomly.

clinicalQuestion: In HR+/HER2-, node-negative breast cancer with a midrange 21-gene recurrence score, can adjuvant chemotherapy be omitted without compromising invasive disease-free survival?

pico.population: Women with HR+/HER2-, axillary node-negative breast cancer and a 21-gene recurrence score of 11-25
pico.comparator: Adjuvant chemotherapy plus endocrine therapy (chemoendocrine therapy)
pico.outcomes: Primary: invasive disease-free survival (non-inferiority). Secondary: distant and locoregional recurrence-free intervals, OS

arms.label: Chemoendocrine therapy
arms.regimen: Adjuvant chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy

publications.title: Adjuvant Chemotherapy Guided by a 21-Gene Expression Assay in Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Endocrine therapy was noninferior to chemoendocrine therapy in the analysis of invasive disease-free survival (hazard ratio for invasive disease recurrence, second primary cancer, or death [endocrine vs. chemoendocrine therapy], 1.08; 95% confidence interval, 0.94 to 1.24; P=0.26). At 9 years, the two treatment groups had similar rates of invasive disease-free survival (83.3% in the endocrine-therapy group and 84.3% in the chemoendocrine-therapy group)

outcomes.endpointLabel: Freedom from distant recurrence at 9 years
outcomes.sourceQuote: At 9 years, the two treatment groups had similar rates of invasive disease-free survival (83.3% in the endocrine-therapy group and 84.3% in the chemoendocrine-therapy group), freedom from disease recurrence at a distant site (94.5% and 95.0%) or at a distant or local-regional site (92.2% and 92.9%), and overall survival (93.9% and 93.8%).

At 9 years, the two treatment groups had similar rates of invasive disease-free survival (83.3% in the endocrine-therapy group and 84.3% in the chemoendocrine-therapy group), freedom from disease recurrence at a distant site (94.5% and 95.0%) or at a distant or local-regional site (92.2% and 92.9%), and overall survival (93.9% and 93.8%).

outcomes.endpointLabel: Interaction of chemotherapy benefit with recurrence score and age
outcomes.population: Women 50 years of age or younger with recurrence score 16 to 25 (benefit signal)
outcomes.sourceQuote: The chemotherapy benefit for invasive disease-free survival varied with the combination of recurrence score and age (P=0.004), with some benefit of chemotherapy found in women 50 years of age or younger with a recurrence score of 16 to 25.

strengths: Very large prospective trial with randomisation of the clinically uncertain midrange recurrence-score group
Long follow-up with a pre-specified non-inferiority design
limitations: Exploratory age/recurrence-score interaction suggesting some chemotherapy benefit in younger women was not the primary comparison

clinicalImplications.text: Supports omitting adjuvant chemotherapy for most women with HR+/HER2-, node-negative breast cancer and a midrange 21-gene recurrence score, while flagging women aged 50 or younger with scores in the upper midrange as a group in whom some chemotherapy benefit was observed.

tumourBoardPearl.text: In node-negative HR+/HER2- disease, the recurrence score must be read together with age/menopausal status: the abstract reports some chemotherapy benefit in women 50 or younger with scores of 16 to 25.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 29860917. Phase III designation and sponsor network reflect the trial's published design; later secondary analyses not ingested.
